reasons.A: Long, evenly joined sentences with a dry, understated irony and a period register that match the passage's genial euphemism (like 'increase the amount of cash in circulation') without overdoing it.
reasons.C: Right period diction and ironic stance, but it ends nearly every paragraph on a polished aphorism and adds an 'I'/'Our young man' narrator the passage doesn't use, so it reads as a thicker imitation.
reasons.B: Short, clipped modern sentences, a plain and confiding tone, and a reflective 'What stays with you' ending, all foreign to the passage's leisurely nineteenth-century irony.
